title: the outline becomes the schematic: requirements/*.md read by the outline check
intention: The outline lives as one markdown file per section in cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/, with a TOC.md saying what each file holds, and the outline check reads that folder.
why: A builder should read a piece, not the whole, which is what devices are for; Akien's scans find the outline more effective than the charters, and it has grown from under 100 lines to 2,100.
traces_to: Law 1 (the settled spec is read, not re-derived) and Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now).
how: Split the outline into requirements/NN-<slug>.md (section top line '# N TITLE', deeper entries as '- <number> <text>' list items indented two spaces per dot past the first), write TOC.md, widen outline_check's ENTRY regex for the markdown marker, read the pieces in filename order, repoint the scratch-outline proofs, remove the .txt.

measured.saw: outline is 2,100 lines / 148 KB in one file; the only code reader of its path is outline_check.py (OUTLINE_HOME, OUTLINE_NAME); 5 proofs write a scratch copy

outcomes.text: D1: the split. One file per top-level section, NN zero-padded, slug from the title. Entry text unchanged; only the marker and indentation change. Fidelity is measured once at build: parse(joined pieces) equals parse(git show a921554bf:press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt), recorded on the verdict.
outcomes.claim: parse() over the requirements pieces joined in filename order yields the same numbered entries, text for text, as parse() over press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt at a921554bf

outcomes.text: D2: TOC.md, one line per piece: link and what it holds, in one phrase.
outcomes.claim: every NN-*.md in the live requirements folder is named in its TOC.md, and every file TOC.md names exists

outcomes.text: D3: outline_check: ENTRY allows a leading '#'/'-'/'*' marker; outline_dir() names the folder; check() reads sorted NN-*.md joined by a blank line; outline_path is the folder, outline_sha256 over the joined bytes.
outcomes.claim: parse() reads the markdown form ('# 9 X', nested '- 9.4.2 text' items with continuation lines) into each numbered entry with its text joined, and check() over a scratch cairn whose cairn/devices/cairn/requirements holds two pieces renders both into the prompt and records the folder as outline_path

outcomes.text: D4: the proofs that write a scratch press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt write a scratch requirements piece instead.
outcomes.claim: the proofs that wrote a scratch press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt write a scratch requirements piece instead, and pass

outcomes.text: D5: remove press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt; outline 0.9 names the folder; press_office/INDEX.md and skills/sorted/SKILL.md point at it.
outcomes.claim: no .py, bin/ or skills/ file outside proofs/ and validations/ names CairnComponentOutline.txt, and press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt is gone

constraints: D6: the proof, one tooth per clause.
